audioScript:
Girl: We went on a class visit to the zoo today. Look at the picture I took.
Man: What a lot of children and animals!
Girl: Can you see Daisy?
Man: No, where is she?
Girl: She's there. She's next to the parrots. She's eating ice cream.
Man: Oh yes.

Man: Who's that girl?
Girl: The girl who's looking at the snakes?
Man: No, the one who's <u>waving at the camels</u>. Who's she?
Girl: That's <u>Sarah</u>.

Man: One person in the photo isn't smiling.
Girl: Oh, who do you mean?
Man: That boy there who's <u>wearing a T-shirt with a dinosaur on it</u>. Who's he?
Girl: That's <u>Harry</u>. He was sad because he lost his camera.
Man: Oh dear.

Man: And who's the <u>blonde boy</u> who's <u>holding the toy camel</u>?
Girl: That's <u>Tom</u>.
Man: Did he buy that camel at the zoo?
Girl: Yes, he did.

Girl: And there's my friend, <u>Vicky</u>.
Man: Is she the girl who's sitting down near the snakes?
Girl: No, Vicky's <u>standing up</u>. She's <u>looking at a map of the zoo</u>.
Man: Oh yes, with the striped shorts.
Girl: Yes, that's her.

Man: Whose dad came with you?
Girl: Vicky's dad came. He's called <u>Peter</u>.
Man: Is he the one talking on the phone?
Girl: No, that's our teacher. Peter is <u>helping Harry with his shoe</u>. He's <u>wearing a green sweater</u>.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: Listen and write. There is one example.
audioScript:
Woman: Good morning, everyone. I have some exciting news. We're going to start a new club at school next year. Ask me some questions about it, then write down what I say.
Boy: What club is it, Mrs Park?
Woman: It's a pet club.

Boy: Wow! It sounds amazing!
Woman: Yes, Robert, I think it will be.
Boy: What animals will there be?
Woman: We're going to get some mice, rabbits and <u>lizards</u>.
Boy: Yes! I love rabbits!

Boy: What day will the club be?
Woman: It's going to be every <u>Thursday</u>.
Boy: Great!

Woman: Anything else you want to know?
Boy: Yes, what time will it be?
Woman: It'll be after school, from <u>4 o'clock</u> to 4.30.
Boy: OK.

Woman: Any more questions?
Boy: Yes, which teacher will do pet club?
Woman: Mr <u>Lewis</u> will be doing pet club. That's L-E-W-I-S.
Boy: OK, I've written that.

Boy: Mrs Park, which classroom will pet club be in?
Woman: It'll be in the <u>science</u> room because that's where the pets will live.
Boy: Great. I can't wait!

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
Helen is helping Dad to get the suitcase ready for their holiday. Where is each thing that she needs to find?
Listen and write a letter in each box. There is one example.
audioScript:
Man: Helen, can you help me get ready for our holiday? We must put everything we need into the suitcase.
Girl: OK, what do you need?
Man: Go and get the camera first. It's on the shelf in my bedroom, the one near my bed.
Girl: OK.

Girl: What else, Dad?
Man: We need our beach <u>towels</u>.
Girl: Where are they?
Man: They're in the <u>cupboard behind the door in the bathroom</u>. Go and get them for me, please.

Man: We need to take the new <u>books</u> that we bought too.
Girl: Oh yes!
Man: They're in the <u>living room, on the little table next to the bookcase</u>. There are three books – can you bring me all of them?
Girl: OK.

Man: OK, what else do we need? Oh yes, I've forgotten to put my <u>glasses</u> in. Can you go and get those for me?
Girl: Where are they, Dad?
Man: They're on my <u>desk, next to the telephone</u>.
Girl: OK. I'll get them now.

Man: Oh, and we don't want to forget the <u>sandwiches</u> that I made for us to eat in the car.
Girl: Have I got jam sandwiches, Dad?
Man: Yes, of course! Now, go and get them for me. I've taken them out of the fridge already. They're on the <u>kitchen table</u>.

Girl: Dad, can I take my favourite <u>doll</u>, Betty?
Man: OK, if you want.
Girl: But I don't know where she is.
Man: She's <u>under the bed in your bedroom</u>. Quickly, go and get her, it's nearly time to go!

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: Listen and tick (✓) the box. There is one example.

items.question: Where does Emma live?
options: in a little village, next to a wood

items.question: What did Jack eat for lunch?
What did the children do in the afternoon?
What time did Jack get home?

audioScript:
Woman: Hi, Jack. You didn't go to school yesterday, did you?
Boy: No, we're on summer holidays.
Woman: Already?! So did you go to the park?
Boy: No, not yesterday. I went to <u>Emma's house</u> to play.

Woman: Oh, great. Did you have fun?
Boy: Yes, lots of fun!
Woman: Where is Emma's house? Does she live in the city?
Boy: No, she doesn't. She lives in a <u>little village, next to a wood</u>.

Woman: And what did you do?
Boy: First, we played with Emma's pet.
Woman: Oh, is Emma the girl with the cat called George?
Boy: No, it's my friend Sally who's got a cat.
Woman: Oh, OK.
Boy: Emma has a <u>rabbit</u> called Carrots.
Woman: That's an excellent name for a rabbit.

Woman: Did Emma's dad make you some lunch?
Boy: Yes, he did. He made some soup. I tasted it, but I didn't like it because it had onions in it.
Woman: Oh dear.
Boy: So, he made me a <u>sandwich</u> and I ate that.
Woman: That was kind of him.

Woman: And what did you do in the afternoon? Did you play in the garden?
Boy: No, it rained, so we stayed inside. We <u>cooked some cakes</u>.
Woman: Great, did you bring some home for me?
Boy: No, sorry! We ate them all!

Woman: Did you get back home very late?
Boy: Yes, Dad came to get me at 8 o'clock and then he was talking to Emma's dad until 8.30. So we didn't get home until <u>9 o'clock</u>.
Woman: Are you very tired today?
Boy: No, not really. I slept until 10 o'clock this morning.

The big duck in the lake
The girl giving bread to the ducks
The boy's shorts (the boy climbing the tree)

audioScript:
Woman: Would you like to colour this picture?
Boy: Yes, please.
Woman: Good, now, can you see the girl with long hair who is on the swing?
Boy: Yes, I can.
Woman: Can you colour her dress <u>purple</u>?
Boy: OK.

Boy: What shall I colour now?
Woman: Can you see the man reading the newspaper at the front of the picture?
Boy: Yes, I can.
Woman: Can you colour his hat <u>green</u>?
Boy: Yes, OK. I'll do that now.

Woman: Would you like to write something?
Boy: Yes, please. What shall I write?
Woman: Now, there's a problem with this picture. Look at the boys playing soccer. Can you see the problem?
Boy: Oh yes, they haven't got a ball. Have they lost it?
Woman: Perhaps. But can you write the word "<u>ball</u>" for them?
Boy: Yes, OK. I'll write it here at their feet. The ball might be here!
Woman: Yes, you're right!

Woman: Now, can you see the ducks in the lake?
Boy: Yes, I can.
Woman: Would you like to colour one of the ducks?
Boy: Yes, but which one? The big one or the little one?
Woman: Colour the big one.
Boy: What colour shall I use?
Woman: Colour the big duck <u>orange</u>.
Boy: OK.

Boy: Can I write something else now?
Woman: Yes, OK. Can you see the girl who is giving some bread to the ducks?
Boy: Yes, those ducks are hungry, aren't they?
Woman: Yes, they are.
Boy: What shall I write?
Woman: Can you write the word "<u>duck</u>" on the girl's dress?
Boy: Yes, of course. That's easy.

Woman: Now for some more colouring.
Boy: OK. Can I colour something pink?
Woman: OK, can you see the boy who is climbing the tree?
Boy: Yes, that looks dangerous, doesn't it?
Woman: You're right. Can you colour his shorts <u>pink</u>?
Boy: OK. I'll do that now.
Woman: Very good. The picture looks excellent now!
